Definition: properly, to draw together the feet (as an animal about to dart upon its prey), i.e. to spring forward
BiblicalUsage: zânaq means properly, to draw together the feet (as an animal about to dart upon its prey), that is to spring forward. In Deuteronomy 33:22 we read, "And of Dan he said, Dan is a lion's whelp: he shall leap from Bashan."
TheologicalSignificance: zanaq is properly, to draw together the feet (as an animal about to dart upon its prey), that is to spring forward, and I hold that even a word used only a few times carries weight where God placed it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
